Is AI Your New Wingman? How Chatbots Are Transforming Modern Dating

02 Nov 2026, 02:21 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Key takeawaysA growing number of singles are turning to artificial intelligence for romantic advice, from drafting messages to evaluating potential partners. According to a survey published by Match Group—the parent company of Tinder and Hinge—nearly 40% of British singles have util

A growing number of singles are turning to artificial intelligence for romantic advice, from drafting messages to evaluating potential partners. According to a survey published by Match Group—the parent company of Tinder and Hinge—nearly 40% of British singles have utilized AI in their dating lives.

Key Findings from the Survey

  • High Adoption Among Youth: AI usage rises sharply among younger demographics, with 66% of Gen Z and 53% of Millennials reporting they have used AI for dating purposes.
  • Common Use Cases: Singles primarily use chatbots to seek advice on conversations, plan dates, draft profiles, and vet whether profiles or photos are genuine.
  • Photo Alteration Boundaries: While text generation is popular, the majority of singles draw the line at using AI to alter their photos.

Practical Implications and User Experiences

Users worldwide report various motivations for employing AI assistants:

  • Confidence and Mentorship: Some individuals use tools like ChatGPT to build relationship security, manage anxiety over delayed messages, and avoid rushing into situations.
  • Streamlining the Search: Older users returning to the dating pool note that AI helps manage the heavy workload of messaging and evaluating matches, occasionally encouraging them to reconsider profiles they initially passed over.
  • Risks and Social Friction: Admissions of AI use can be risky; approximately one-third of UK singles surveyed stated they would end a date if they discovered AI was used to write messages.

Industry Stance and Future Outlook

While some users express interest in future concepts like autonomous AI assistants communicating with each other before humans interact, platforms are pushing back. Match Group's head of trust and safety, Yoel Roth, emphasized a firm stance against bot-to-bot dating, stating that authentic human connection cannot be achieved by letting robots converse on behalf of people.

How to Verify

To verify these claims and review the underlying data, readers can consult official reports published by Match Group or reference original reporting on the shifting landscape of digital relationships.
